strategy.label: vintage transfer: the ecoinvent v2 unit process of the same product, transcribed from its report table and verified against the two co-products BAFU still carries
strategy.note: The cited report (Rajabihamedani 2025) prints no unit process - it documents only the post-processing of a PlasticsEurope system process (see specs/evidence/582ad303-.../response-0-locate.json). The inventory here is transcribed from Althaus 2007, ecoinvent report No. 8, Tab. 35.3, which documents the multi-output process 'ethylene oxide, in ethylene glycol plant' that ecoinvent v2 used for this same dataset name, and allocated to MEG with the report's own 85 % price-times-mass factor over its 0.825 kg of MEG. The transcription is verified, not assumed: applying the same table with the DEG factor (7 %/0.1 kg) and the TEG factor (8 %/0.04 kg) reproduces BAFU's own 'Diethylene glycol, at plant' and 'Triethylene glycol, at plant' unit processes on all eleven exchanges the table covers - exactly on nine of them (ethylene oxide 0.4921 kg, electricity 0.2639 kWh, chemical plant 2.8E-10, waste heat 0.945 MJ, acetaldehyde 9.8E-07, ethylene 4.2E-06, water 0.0042 m3, and the TEG column 1.406 / 0.754 / 8E-10) and to 0.15 % on the two four-digit ones (COD/BOD 2.013E-04 against 2.016E-04, TOC/DOC 5.248E-05 against 5.250E-05). The twelfth exchange, the waterborne water emission, is not in Tab. 35.3 at all and is taken from the co-products' own 0.95 ratio. This is S2 and not S1 because the BAFU dataset being rebuilt is the PlasticsEurope 2019 eco-profile (reference year 2023), a different data generation from the 1997-2000 ecoinvent v2 inventory transcribed here; the structure is the same product's, the vintage is not. Steam is calibrated because Tab. 35.3 omits it and sec. 35.6.2 says so explicitly, and the infrastructure is calibrated between 0 and the transcribed 4.1212E-10 because the ethylene-oxide precursor already carries one chemical plant of its own.

evidence.where: Tab. 35.3 (printed p. 307, PDF p. 388), ch. 35 Ethylene Glycol
evidence.note: Multi-output process 'ethylene oxide, in ethylene glycol plant' [RER], per 1 kg: ethylene oxide, at plant 7.03E-1 kg; electricity, medium voltage, production UCTE, at grid 3.77E-1 kWh; chemical plant, organics 4.00E-10 unit; Water, unspecified natural origin 6.00E-03 m3; Heat, waste 1.35E+00 MJ; Acetaldehyde 1.40E-06 kg; Ethene 6.00E-06 kg; BOD5 2.88E-04 kg; COD 2.88E-01 kg (see note below); DOC 7.50E-05 kg; TOC 7.50E-05 kg. Outputs diethylene glycol 0.1 kg, ethylene glycol 0.825 kg, triethylene glycol 0.04 kg, with the allocation row 7 / 85 / 8 %. Every amount below is that column times 0.85/0.825 = 1.030303.

'It is assumed that an average 82.5% of the glycols consists of MEG. This report assumes that a further 10% is DEG, the remainder being TEG and heavy glycols.' Tab. 35.2 gives Input: Ethylene oxide 703, Output: MEG 825, DEG 100, TEG 40, Heavy glycols 35 (kg), with price x mass allocation factors 85 / 7 / 8 %. Sec. 35.5 notes the wider IPPC range: 'the glycol products typically consists of 70 - 95% w/w of MEG' - the 82.5 % split is one point in it.

'It must be assumed that some steam is utilized for glycol distillation. No figures are given. Electrical energy consumption is given as 0.377 kWh / kg in (BUWAL 232).' The steam input is therefore in the model but calibrated, unbounded - the report names it and refuses to quantify it.

evidence.source: bafu-2026: Diethylene glycol, at plant [RER] and Triethylene glycol, at plant [RER]
evidence.note: Both are 3-input unit processes still in BAFU-2026 and are the co-products of the very table transcribed here. Tab. 35.3 x 0.07/0.1 gives ethylene oxide 0.4921 kg, electricity 0.2639 kWh, chemical plant 2.80E-10 unit, water 0.0042 m3, waste heat 0.945 MJ, acetaldehyde 9.8E-07, ethylene 4.2E-06, BOD 2.016E-04, COD 2.016E-04, DOC/TOC 5.25E-05 - which is exactly what BAFU's DEG carries (0.4921 / 0.2639 / 2.8E-10 / 0.0042 / 0.945 / 9.8E-07 / 4.2E-06 / 2.013E-04 / 2.013E-04 / 5.248E-05). Same for TEG at 0.08/0.04 (EO 1.406, electricity 0.754, plant 8E-10). Two consequences: the transcription is verified, and the report's COD of 2.88E-01 kg is a typo for 2.88E-04 (the co-products carry BOD = COD), which is what is used here. The co-products also fix the water balance, 0.00399/0.0042 = 0.95 of the water input leaving as a waterborne emission; Tab. 35.3 gives only the input.

'For all datasets, the inventory regarding infrastructure contributions was checked and supplemented. For the implementation, the dataset "Chemical plant, organics {RER}U" is used. The quantity is the standard amount for production of chemicals of 4.0E-10 p.' The BAFU target indeed carries 4.0E-10 p, and Tab. 35.3 gives the same 4.00E-10 unit - the two vintages agree on this one input.

node.name: Ethylene glycol, at plant, disaggregated
node.comment: Unit process of the glycol section of an integrated EO/EG plant, per kg of MEG. Althaus 2007 Tab. 35.3 x 0.85/0.825. Steam calibrated (the report names it and gives no figure). The waste-treatment services and the infrastructure that BAFU's own aggregated dataset already carries explicitly are deliberately NOT copied into this model except for the infrastructure the report states; the point of the rebuild is the production chain, which is the part that was collapsed away.

inputs.name: Ethylene oxide, at plant
inputs.note: Tab. 35.3 'ethylene oxide, at plant' 7.03E-01 kg x 0.85/0.825; precursor, reaction (2) C2H4O + H2O -> HO-C2H4-OH

inputs.name: Electricity, medium voltage, production ENTSO-E, at grid
inputs.note: Tab. 35.3 'electricity, medium voltage, production UCTE, at grid' 3.77E-01 kWh x 0.85/0.825 (BUWAL 232); UCTE -> the ENTSO-E successor dataset BAFU carries

inputs.name: Chemical plant, organics
inputs.note: Tab. 35.3 4.00E-10 unit x 0.85/0.825 = 4.1212E-10, and Rajabihamedani sec. 3.6 gives the same 4.0E-10 p for the target - both vintages agree on it, which is why that is the upper bound. It is a bound and not the amount because 'Ethylene oxide, at plant' already carries its own 4.0E-10, and this one exchange is where 1316 of the target's 1790 cumulative flows get more than 90 % of their value from, so stacking two doubles three quarters of the vector; the fit decides how much of it belongs here (see scripts/plasticseurope_infrastructure_diagnostic.py).

inputs.name: Steam, for chemical processes, at plant
inputs.note: sec. 35.6.2: 'It must be assumed that some steam is utilized for glycol distillation. No figures are given.' Named by the report, not quantified -> calibrated, unbounded. The 0.5 start value is arbitrary and is overwritten by the fit.
